info.name: Hotstar Live — REST read edge (design [D])
info.description: Buildable [D] REST contract for the Hotstar live-streaming design in system-designs-with-deva/hotstar. NOT the real (unpublished) Hotstar/JioHotstar playback API — the public read edge you'd build, faithful to the on-screen decisions: cacheable-vs-must-compute is the axis (immutable year-cached segments = the 70-Tbps road; scorecard/concurrency s-maxage + stale-while-revalidate; only POST /playback/session and GET /entitlement must-compute), signed short-TTL manifest URLs, DRM = multi-DRM trio (vendor UNKNOWN), emoji fire-and-forget 202 (no idempotency, relaxed correctness). The MQTT realtime spine (50M sockets, QoS 0) is NOT in this collection — Postman collections don't carry MQTT; see api-contracts.md §3. Set {{apiUrl}} to a mock server. See api-contracts.md.

request.description: The ONLY origin round-trip in the happy path. Checks auth + entitlement + concurrency, then mints a signed short-TTL manifest URL + DRM handshake. Returns 200 { sessionId, manifestUrl (signed, ~45s TTL), cohort, drm (vendor UNKNOWN), concurrency, asOf }. Cache-Control: private, no-store. 401/403 not entitled · 409 device-concurrency cap · 451 geo-blocked · 503 panic-mode (retry w/ jitter).

item.name: GET master.m3u8 — the manifest (signed, short-cached, SSAI-stitched)

query.description: short TTL (~30-60s); expired -> 403 at edge, no origin call

request.description: Fetched with the signed URL from /playback/session. Returns the HLS master playlist (rendition ladder ~200kbps -> ~5Mbps, exact rungs UNKNOWN) with SSAI already stitched server-side at SCTE-35 markers for this cohort. Media playlists carry #EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY at ad seams. Still a file -> Cache-Control: public, max-age=2. No Authorization: the signed manifest is the capability, DRM is the content lock.

item.name: GET seg*.ts — the segment (immutable, edge-served, 70-Tbps road)

request.description: The bytes. Immutable content cached for a year -> Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable; X-Cache: HIT. No auth on the segment (signed manifest gated entry, DRM locks content). >90% served as a CDN cache HIT that never touches origin. This single immutable header is why 72M players requesting the same ball hit the edge, not your origin — the 60-80 Tbps number survivable.

header.description: cheap 304 revalidation for the chatty widget

request.description: A chatty widget read by millions. Freshness deliberately relaxed. Returns 200 { score, batting, lastEvent, asOf, stale: true } or 304 on matching If-None-Match. Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=3, stale-while-revalidate=10; ETag echoed. stale:true + asOf say out loud the number may have moved.

The social layer. Correctness DELIBERATELY relaxed: NO idempotency key, NO durable ack. Client batches reactions and fires; edge returns 202 { accepted, note } and never blocks playback. Cache-Control: no-store. Ingest Go -> Kafka (500ms) -> Spark (2s) -> MQTT fanout (QoS 0). Delivery back to clients is MQTT (api-contracts.md §3), not HTTP.
Returns { entitled, plan, deviceLimit, reason }. Cache-Control: private, max-age=30. A P0 read — panic-mode keeps auth/subscription alive while recs/watchlist die first.

Returns { concurrent: 72500000, metric: CONCURRENCY, note: NOT cumulative views, asOf }. Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=5, stale-while-revalidate=15; X-Metric-Kind: CONCURRENCY. The metric/X-Metric-Kind fields put the metric-trap guardrail on the wire — concurrency, never cumulative views.
